agent_notes: Two distinct threads exist under the same name: (1) Kumbhana the Dhatarwal Jat farming village, founded by Kumbha son of Nathu Dhatarwal, displaced 1984-85 for the Mahajan Field Firing Range — confirmed directly by a Rajasthan Patrika 2022 feature quoting a Kumbhana-born businessman about the Holika-burning tradition still kept alive on-site; and (2) Kumbhana the Rathore (Ratansinghot) Thikana of Bikaner state, ranked just below Mahajan, documented in detail on rajputs.net/indianrajputs.com and jatland.com. Direct WebFetch of jatland.com/home/Kumbhana returned HTTP 403 (site blocks the fetcher), so that content is only available via the WebSearch AI-summary — flagged for re-verification. Village-level census/gov data (census2011, villageinfo.in) could not be isolated: those sites index a different 'Kumbhana' in Harij, Patan, Gujarat, and a direct URL guess for the Bikaner one 403'd. No YouTube, Facebook/Instagram, or dedicated image results specific to this village turned up despite several query variants — likely subsumed under generic 'Mahajan Field Firing Range' or 'Bikaner village' content rather than named separately. Spelling variants that mattered: Hindi कुम्भाणा is stable across sources; one search auto-corrected to 'Kumhana' in a village-list sentence, so that variant is worth trying too.
